# Short-recording loudnorm histogram regression

`loudnorm-histogram.wav` and `loudnorm-histogram.y4m` form a synthetic half-second
audio/video pair, generated by `scripts/generate_loudnorm_sample.py` without
FFmpeg, external encoders or private media. Audio is mono signed 16-bit PCM at
192 kHz, alternating +328/-328; video has 15 black/white 16x16 frames at 30 fps.

The newly implemented normalizer initially derived gain from exact accumulated
energy. Its reference behavior derives gain from 0.1 LU histogram bin centers.
This fixture distinguishes those decisions without resampling or codec errors.
The intended result is accepted by the public `apply_loudnorm` regression test;
it is not an unsupported-feature refusal test.

For a Nyquist square wave, the shelf magnitude is
`h = 10^(3.999843853973347/20)` and the high-pass magnitude is
`d = 1 + k/0.5003270373238773 + k²`, with
`k = tan(pi*38.13547087602444/192000)`. The weighted steady level is
`-0.691 + 20*log10((328/32768)*h*d) = -36.67185 LUFS`, well inside the
[-36.7, -36.6) bin. The independent expected gain for target -16 LUFS is
`10^((-16+36.65)/20)`, producing float32 samples of +/-0.10787577.

Ordinary tests read the checked-in files and invoke no generator or external
reference process. The explicit `ffmpeg_short_loudnorm_reference` benchmark
also compares this acceptance fixture with an external reference, separately
from the ordinary test suite.

## Long-recording acceptance

`loudnorm-dynamic.wav` and `loudnorm-dynamic.y4m` are a second synthetic
three-second pair generated by the same script. Audio is 192 kHz mono signed
16-bit PCM, alternating signs with amplitudes 64, 4096 and 512 in consecutive
one-second ranges. Video is 90 16x16 Y4M frames at 30 fps. Exactly three seconds
previously reached the owned long-form refusal; the public regression now
accepts it, checks frame count/order, integrated loudness, the FIR true-peak
ceiling and pre-allocation memory admission. Tests read existing fixtures;
they do not run the generator or a reference codec.

Additional analytic tests exercise a 12-second dynamic-range input and linked
stereo impulses at the beginning, middle and final frame. The explicit
`ffmpeg_dynamic_loudnorm_reference` benchmark reports target and timing
measurements for both algorithms. Dynamic PCM equivalence is not its contract.

## Limiter feedback regression

`loudnorm-feedback.wav` and `loudnorm-feedback.y4m` form a synthetic three-second
pair: a 1 kHz PCM16 background at amplitude 0.03 with isolated ~0.9 impulses at
0.5, 1.5 and 2.5 seconds. An initial single limiter pass left unused headroom
between peaks and missed the requested I target. Bounded loudness feedback now
recovers that headroom while rechecking the true-peak ceiling. The acceptance
test checks I within 0.2 LU, TP <= -1.5 dBTP and exact sample count. It uses no
external reference. Both pairs are generated by `generate_loudnorm_sample.py`.

## Owned dual-pass acceptance

`loudnorm-dual.wav` and `loudnorm-dual.y4m` are generated independently by
`generate_loudnorm_sample.py`: eight seconds of 48 kHz mono PCM16 with a 1 kHz
sine changing amplitude from 0.03 to 0.06 at four seconds, paired with 240
16x16 Y4M frames. Nonzero LRA and sufficient peak headroom select linear
normalization. The native CLI acceptance checks original rate and duration,
target loudness, true-peak ceiling, JSON reporting and monotonic two-pass
progress with one completion event. A separate regression cancels at the end
of measurement and verifies that no destination is published. The three-second
zero-LRA fixture verifies dynamic fallback. Tests never run the generator or
FFmpeg.

The public `fvid_media::plan_loudnorm` API also uses this fixture to verify
owned WAVE planning with and without the legacy feature. Single/dual-pass
plans share execution parameter validation, report selection and PCM block
limit semantics. Planning reads metadata only, emits no progress, and describes
the owned controller rather than a libavfilter graph. The native CLI delegates
its WAVE plan to this same library API.
